means: A heavy, high-contrast keyline around characters and props - the ink weight of the drawing, independent of how it is coloured.
does: Bolds the character keyline and separates figures hard from the background. Reads punchy and shounen. The tested clause is 'thick lineart, bold heavy outlines' and it does register - but studio/cards/anime_draw_line_weight.json measured that there is NO degree control at the other end: 'extremely thin lineart, hairline outlines' and 'thin lineart, delicate outlines' render identically, because the model has one thin-lineart feature and no fine gradation on it. So thick versus normal is a real switch; fine weight steps are not.
reach_for_it: when figures are getting lost against a busy background, or when you want the frame to read as TV animation rather than as illustration
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
